documents.title: Contextual Embeddings: Implementing Bound Variables Through Instance Resolution

topics.name: Types and contexts
topics.description: Guest types and snoc contexts specify the types and available variables of the simply typed lambda calculus.

topics.name: Typed de Bruijn indices
topics.description: Top and Pop locate a variable of a given type within its context.

topics.name: First-order terms
topics.description: Variables, abstraction, application and the unit term form the first-order embedding.

topics.name: Singleton variable markers
topics.description: A singleton marker saves the context and type of the most recently introduced variable.

topics.name: Context extension
topics.description: The identity and extension instances recover a de Bruijn index from the binding and use contexts.

topics.name: Contextual terms
topics.description: Contextual terms use host functions for abstraction and reification for variable occurrences.

topics.name: Unembedding contextual terms
topics.description: Unembedding translates contextual syntax to first-order syntax while preserving context and guest type.

topics.name: Contextualising first-order terms
topics.description: Contextualisation translates first-order syntax back to contextual syntax.

topics.name: Converting individual variables
topics.description: An existential variable package separates conversion of indices from conversion of whole terms.

topics.name: Term round trips
topics.description: The two term equations express recovery of the original representation after both conversions.

topics.name: Index round trips
topics.description: The variable equations relate de Bruijn indices to their existential packages and support the term equations.

topics.name: Closed world assumption
topics.description: The reverse conversion relies on the assumption that reification uses only the identity and context-extension instances.
